text:
zoe: seeing repeated p99 spikes on /v1/embeddings in eu-west after yesterday's CUDA15+driver push. multiple customers reporting tighter SLO breaches. logs show long tail in token generation step.

jamal: thanks, starting triage. is this across Dedicated and Hosted?

zoe: hosted only so far (shared pool). Dedicated seats unaffected for now.

scott: any correlating infra changes? kernel/drivers/firmware?

zoe: rollout notes show CUDA 15.0.1 + driver 540.20 applied to eu-west workers at 02:10 UTC. kernel stable. NVMe firmware update wasn't part of this rollout.

maya-support: customer ACME reported p95->p99 jump from 120ms->800ms around 02:25 UTC, repeated over next hour. attached traces show long waits in host IO: "io_wait_us" high during generation.

jamal: running a quick grep on traces. looks like long stall during KV cache lookup step (mini-checkpoint read). sample stack:
```
kernel: block_rq_issue -> nvme_submit -> nvme_wait -> __switch_to
user: app -> runtime_kv_read -> wait_for_io
```

scott: that suggests cooperative scheduling + new driver I/O path causing tail. We saw similar with CUDA14 rollouts but different stack.

oncall: infra-bot reports io.qdepth spiking on host 10.23.4.17 at 02:22 UTC, qdepth peaked ~128, latency distribution tail at p99 ~1.1s.

ops-jen: I can repro locally on a small repro harness by replaying customer workload against eu-west AMI with CUDA15. Repro script: `python tools/repro/replay_workload.py --workload acme-embed-2026-03 --workers 4` yields p99 ~900ms within 10 minutes.

zoe: good repro. what's different vs pre-rollout?

ops-jen: observed increased NVMe submission latency for small random reads; profiling shows extra futex wait in io completion path when GPU driver is doing page pinning concurrently.

scott: hypothesis: new driver + CUDA15 changed UMA/pinning behavior causing occasional host-side stalls under concurrent NVMe IO and GPU pin/unpin. That can amplify tail for small KV cache reads.

jamal: mitigation options: 1) pin rollback of driver on affected hosts, 2) throttle concurrency on embeds (reduce in-flight requests / increase per-host token budget), 3) enable local in-memory KV warm cache to avoid NVMe reads.

maya-support: customer-facing mitigation — can we route ACME to Dedicated or a non-upgraded pool temporarily? they'll accept a stopgap.

oncall: can do immediate routing: adding a rule to route `model:embed-*` for tenant=acme to eu-west-oldpool. Command: `rb route add --tenant acme --pool eu-west-oldpool --match "embed" --priority 900`.

ops-jen: deployed routing rule. ACME confirms reduced p99 to ~150ms after 3 mins.

scott: good. longer-term: we should throttle page-pinning concurrency in the runtime (limit GPU mmap/munmap concurrency) and coordinate with driver vendor. Also add host-level cgroup IO weighting so KV reads get priority over bulk GPU-offload IO.

jamal: filing infra ticket to roll back driver on a canary subset and run bisect. ticket: INFRA-6227. assigning to scott/ops-jen.

zoe: also adding a temporary runtime knob `--max-pin-concurrency=12` to reduce munmap storms. Ops post-deploy required.

ops-jen: pushed runtime flag to eu-west canary hosts, monitoring.

infra-bot: deploy succeeded on canary group (hosts 10.23.4.16-18).

scott: monitoring shows p99 on repro harness dropped from 900ms -> 180ms after the flag. promising.

maya-support: sending customer update: workaround applied (routing -> oldpool). asking to keep them updated on driver rollback plan. :thumbsup:

jamal: next steps: 1) bisect driver changes with vendor, 2) prepare rollback plan if bisect points to driver, 3) implement runtime pinning throttle and cgroup IO priorities cluster-wide as a safety net, 4) add KV cache hit telemetry to better correlate in future.

zoe: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate postmortem and customer note. please add any logs/traces to INFRA-6227.

scott: adding playbook snippet for future:
```
# triage steps
1. confirm scope (hosted/dedicated)
2. grep traces for kv_read/io_wait
3. check io.qdepth and nvme latency
4. route affected tenants to older pool
5. deploy --max-pin-concurrency to canary
6. bisect driver versions
```

jamal: marking incident severity: sev3 for ongoing mitigation, escalate to sev2 if customer SLOs continue to be violated after routing.

zoe: noted. last update: 1809992700 — routing applied, canary flag rolled, customer routed. closing active paging but keeping ticket open for bisect/rollback.
